newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela govt workers to strike till bonuses paid.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela govt workers to strike till bonuses paid.

text.p: A strike by thousands of Venezuelan civil servants went into its ninth day Thursday in spite of assurances from President Rafael Caldera that their pay demands would be met.
Union leaders met with Caldera late Thursday, but said they would believe his promises that delayed salary bonuses would be met only when they received the money.

"I am convinced that between now and Monday the money won't be paid," Israel Coromil, executive secretary of the Public Sector Workers Federation, which represents about 1.3 million government workers.
The strike, billed as a 48-hour stoppage when it started on Tuesday, is the most serious labor conflict since President Rafael Caldera took office in February 1994.

Caldera's cabinet of ministers approved extra spending of 30 billion bolivars ($64 million) on Wednesday to meet the bonuses, but union leaders said the government owed workers 100 billion bolivars ($212 million).
"What worries me is that they are 70 billion bolivars short," Coromil said.

Caldera's government is facing an increasing number of year-end protests and strikes as the effects of a gaping recession cut deeply into living standards. Public sector workers earn an average of $106 per month.
